notes: PLAN.md tier 9 section 9.3, class EX: no Python counterpart. This tiny committed fixture is a mechanics sanity check (argument parsing, cool loading, exit status, no crash), not a statistical validation; the recall and precision gate of PLAN.md 9.3 is measured on real GM12878 data by cpp/scripts/stripe_calibration.py, which is far too large to commit (cpp/AGENTS_CONTRACT.md rule 10 and PLAN.md 9.3's 'don't commit large data'). The output is not declared, because small_test_matrix.cool at these lenient thresholds still calls nothing (checked): its chromosomes are too short and too sparse to support the local background window this tool needs, which is expected of a fixture built for other tools' equivalence tests rather than for stripe recovery.

As the cool case above, but through the h5 whole-matrix loader (no per-chromosome band reader for h5, cpp/tools/hicDetectStripes.cpp mirrors hicDetectLoops' approach: hicx::read_hicexplorer_h5 then hicx::select_bins).

Every chromosome of the fixture, default statistical thresholds, at --threads 2 (also exercised at --threads 1 and --threads 4 by --determinism). Checks that the multi-chromosome loop and the short chromosomes some of this fixture's entries have (a handful of bins) do not crash the band builder.
An unknown --chromosomes name exits 1 before anything is written, the same behaviour hicDetectLoops.cpp has for the same condition.

--maxStripeLength below --minStripeLength is refused before any input is read, matching cpp/AGENTS_CONTRACT.md rule 7's 'wrong environment/arguments exit before any output is created' for the argument-level case.
